scope: Operational sending gates, not blanket country legal conclusions

sources.observation: UEC policy covers UAE-linked communications, defines unconsented marketing as spam and requires licensees to minimise transmission. Consent principles apply to licensee customer agreements; mobile annex governs SMS. Do not assert a universal criminal email ban from this policy.
Official government overview states personal-data processing generally requires consent, with exceptions; prospect-specific applicability and lawful basis require verification.

countries.decision: No send until consent or a verified applicable lawful route is documented.

sources.observation: PDPL implementing regulation Articles 28-29 require documented consent for advertising without prior interaction and direct marketing using personal data; identity and withdrawal required.

countries.decision: Prior permission and contact/channel applicability must be documented. Public named business email is not consent.

sources.observation: NCSA-hosted English translation Article 22 requires prior consent for electronic direct marketing to an individual and sender identity/marketing label/opt-out address. Translation says Official Gazette Arabic version controls.

countries.decision: Prior permission required for covered individuals; no assumed general-mailbox exemption. Verify official Arabic text/applicability if needed.

sources.observation: Official MTCIT FAQ requires documentable written consent before commercial advertising/marketing to a data subject; immediate free opt-out.
Official index lists September 2026 PDPL amendment; latest consolidated requirements still need review.

countries.decision: No send until current recipient-specific consent and current amended-law review complete.
